title: Nine Words of Ink
subtitle: 卡片与卡证 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 卡片与卡证（社会服务与人际沟通·消费与证件）
meta: 主题语境：卡片与卡证（社会服务与人际沟通·消费与证件）　|　核心词汇：card　|　正文 340 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 card 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1953 my mother was sent to sign ① a card she could not read, and she said the reading was the whole of the lesson. The ② card, meaning the paper and not the message, was nine words long and was signed by whoever came last; a card, she said, is the only thing in a drawer that is judged by how much has been taken out of it.

Every ③ card in that drawer had the same edge, and the ④ card at the front, meaning the one the clerk kept and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever signed properly. A card, my grandmother said, is nine parts ink and one part somebody willing to stay behind; my mother said the ink is the part that gets everywhere.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ card was the whole of the greeting, meaning the words it carried and not the paper. The ⑥ card, meaning the greeting and not any of that, is the only thing in a house that everybody keeps and nobody questions; a card, he said, is either something you sign or the only word that means both a paper and a greeting. She said the greeting is the part they remember.

By 1969 the ⑦ card had become a photograph in a report, and the report had become an argument about the edge. The ⑧ card of the whole thing, my mother wrote in April, was nine words and eleven years of signing; a card, she said, is either the one at the front or the reason you learned to stand on a chair. He said the chair was never mentioned.

The ⑨ card I remember is the one at the front, which was posted in 1974 and is still described as the best in the county. A ⑩ card, my grandmother said in 1979, is the only thing that improves by being signed; every card, she said, is a greeting that has agreed to look like a paper. She said the greeting was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 卡片（指那张纸本身，与留言相对）
C. 固定搭配：sign a card 在卡片上签名
D. n. 卡片（指抽屉里每一张）
E. n. 卡片（指前面那一张）
F. n. 贺卡（抽象：它承载的那句问候）
G. n. 那句问候（抽象：那件事本身）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: a card she could not read
The card, meaning the paper and not the message
card was the whole of the greeting
the card had become a photograph in a report
The card of the whole thing
A card, my grandmother said in 1979

answers.why: sign a card 意为“在卡片上签名”，1953 年母亲被派去在一张她读不懂的卡片上签名。
card 意为“卡片”，指那张纸本身而不是留言，共九个词，由最后走的人签上名。
card 指抽屉里每一张卡片，每一张都是同样的边。
card 指前面那一张（店员留的那一张），是唯一有人认真签过的。
card 意为“贺卡”，抽象指它承载的那句问候，父亲说 card 就是那句问候的全部。
card 为抽象用法，指那句问候本身，是屋子里人人都留着、却没人质疑的东西。
card 意为“卡片、贺卡”，到 1969 年这张 card 成了报告里的一张照片。
card 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，母亲四月写道，整件事权衡下来是九个词和十一年的签名。
card 意为“卡片”，我记得的是前面那一张，1974 年寄出，至今仍被说成全县最好的。
card 为抽象总称，祖母说卡片是唯一会因为被签上名字而变好的东西。
